title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Auditorium on 1967-11-10
lineage: MR > R > R > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a blistering 1967 set – Viola Lee Blues, Pigpen’s rap, Alligator > Caution and an incendiary Other One.
ai_review.review: The recording is widely praised for its pristine, almost studio‑level clarity with a perfect mix that lets every instrument be heard, despite the occasional vintage hiss or a minor glitch in Viola Lee. Musically the show is hailed as one of ’67’s finest – a scorching opener with Viola Lee Blues, powerful Pigpen moments, a legendary Alligator > Caution marathon and a soaring Other One, all delivered by a band on fire. The energy builds seamlessly from the bluesy start to the psychedelic climax, making it a must‑have for any Dead collector.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews uniformly praise both performance and audio quality; show is described as “one of the best ’67 shows” and recording as “crystal‑clear” with only minor issues, yielding an exceptional combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear mix, balanced levels, very little noise; occasional vintage hiss and a noted glitch around 8:30 in Viola Lee Blues but not detracting from overall listenability.

poor_songs: Cryptical/Other One (one reviewer called it sloppier than usual)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set launches with a bluesy Viola Lee, builds through Pigpen’s rap and tight jams, peaks in the marathon Alligator > Caution, then rolls into an ecstatic Other One, delivering a seamless high‑energy arc typical of peak ’67 performances.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for fierce, razor‑sharp guitar tone (Les Paul) and incendiary solos on Viola Lee, Morning Dew and the Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: His walking bass is highlighted as clear and prominent; several reviewers note “Phil’s bass can be clearly heard”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ/harmonica/vocals receive glowing remarks – “classic performance”, “great Pigpen”.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and newcomer Mickey Hart are lauded for tight, complementary playing; dueling‑drummer dynamics especially noted in Caution.
